- `image_size` · default `1K` · värden: `512`, `1K`, `2K`, `4K` — Output resolution. Nano Banana 2 (gemini-3.1-flash-image-preview): 512, 1K, 2K, 4K. Nano Banana Pro (gemini-3-pro-image-preview) and Imagen: 1K, 2K, 4K. Not supported by gemini-2.5-flash-image.

- `PROMPT` · **obligatorisk** — Text prompt for the Gemini model
- `safety_filter_level` · default `BLOCK_ONLY_HIGH` · värden: `BLOCK_LOW_AND_ABOVE`, `BLOCK_MEDIUM_AND_ABOVE`, `BLOCK_ONLY_HIGH`, `BLOCK_NONE` — Content safety filter level

- `top_k` · default `64` — Top-K sampling: number of highest probability tokens to consider (max 64)
- `top_p` · default `0.95` — Nucleus sampling: cumulative probability cutoff (0-1)

**AI context:**

> The active backend is `gemini-2.5-flash-image`, which does **not** support `image_size` — that parameter is silently ignored on this model, so don't set user expectations around resolution control; direct users who need 2K/4K output to a Pro-tier variant instead. `number_of_images` defaults to 4, so set it to 1 explicitly if the user only wants a single result (saves cost at $0.09/request flat regardless of count). `negative_prompt` is worth using for style exclusions but has limited reliability on flash-class Gemini models compared to dedicated diffusion pipelines — treat it as a soft hint. `temperature`, `top_k`, and `top_p` affect the text-decoding stage rather than the image diffusion directly; they're rarely worth tuning and the defaults are sensible. `person_generation` is hard-blocked at `allow_adult` for EU/UK/CH/MENA regions regardless of what's passed, so warn users in those regions that `allow_all` will fail. Prefer this endpoint over heavier alternatives when throughput and turnaround speed matter more than maximum resolution, or when the prompt requires legible in-image text, which is a noted strength of the Gemini image stack.

- `image_size` · default `1K` · värden: `512`, `1K`, `2K`, `4K` — Output resolution. Nano Banana 2 (gemini-3.1-flash-image-preview): 512, 1K, 2K, 4K. Nano Banana Pro (gemini-3-pro-image-preview) and Imagen: 1K, 2K, 4K. Not supported by gemini-2.5-flash-image.

- `PROMPT` · **obligatorisk** — Text prompt for the Gemini model

> Backed by `gemini-3.1-flash-image-preview`, this is the go-to choice when you want Gemini-quality image generation or editing at a lower cost than Pro-tier alternatives — it supports both text-to-image and image-in/image-out editing workflows in a single call. The flat $0.05/request price covers up to 4 images, so leaving `number_of_images` at its default of 4 is almost always the right call unless you only need one. `image_size` defaults to 1K; 2K is a sweet spot for quality vs. latency — 4K adds noticeable generation time. `aspect_ratio` is the most impactful parameter for most use cases; pair it intentionally with your prompt (e.g. `16:9` for landscapes, `9:16` for mobile-first content). `temperature`, `top_k`, and `top_p` rarely need adjustment for image generation — these are more relevant if the model is producing interleaved text, which this endpoint strips out (`response_type: image`). `person_generation` defaults to `allow_adult` but silently falls back to `allow_adult` if `allow_all` is requested from EU/UK/CH/MENA regions — worth flagging to users building people-centric apps who might not understand why results differ by region.

<a id="nano-banana-pro"></a>
### Nano Banana Pro

- **Slug:** `nano-banana-pro` · **Modell:** `gemini-3-pro-image-preview` · **Kategori:** Image Generation
- **Pris:** $0.15 per anrop · **Max bilder in:** 4 · **Aktiv:** ja
- **Beskrivning:** a state-of-the-art image generation and editing model built on Gemini 3 Pro, designed for professional asset production, high-fidelity visual design, and complex, multi-turn instruction following. It enables advanced features like native 2K/4K rendering, precise text generation within images, and consistent character creation across multiple scenes
- **Konfiguration** (`workflow_json`, utom modell):

  ```json
  {
    "prompt": "",
    "response_type": "image"
  }
  ```

**Parametrar:**

- `aspect_ratio` · default `1:1` · värden: `1:1`, `3:4`, `4:3`, `9:16`, `16:9` — Aspect ratio of the generated image
- `image_size` · default `1K` · värden: `1K`, `2K`, `4K` — Output resolution (Standard/Ultra models only)
- `max_output_tokens` — Maximum output tokens (up to 32,768)
- `negative_prompt` — Elements or styles to exclude from the generated image
- `PROMPT` · **obligatorisk** — Text prompt for the Gemini model
- `safety_filter_level` · default `BLOCK_ONLY_HIGH` · värden: `BLOCK_LOW_AND_ABOVE`, `BLOCK_MEDIUM_AND_ABOVE`, `BLOCK_ONLY_HIGH`, `BLOCK_NONE` — Content safety filter level
- `temperature` · default `1` — Controls randomness (0 = deterministic, max 1)
- `top_k` · default `64` — Top-K sampling: number of highest probability tokens to consider (max 64)
- `top_p` · default `0.95` — Nucleus sampling: cumulative probability cutoff (0-1)

**AI context:**

> Backed by `gemini-3-pro-image-preview`, which is still in preview and can occasionally refuse or degrade on complex compositions — if a request fails, simplifying the prompt or loosening `safety_filter_level` to `BLOCK_ONLY_HIGH` (the default) is the first thing to try. The `image_size` parameter is what unlocks 2K/4K output, but note the label says "Standard/Ultra models only" — in practice, 2K and 4K are available here and are the main reason to choose this endpoint over cheaper alternatives; don't leave it at 1K for professional asset work. `temperature` at the default of 1 produces the most creative variance; drop it toward 0.3–0.5 for product shots or character consistency across scenes where repeatability matters. `top_k` and `top_p` are rarely worth touching — the defaults (64 / 0.95) are well-tuned for this model and adjusting them without also changing `temperature` usually has negligible effect. `max_output_tokens` controls the text reasoning pass, not image resolution — leave it alone unless you're doing heavy multi-turn instruction chaining where the model needs more room to plan. Prefer this endpoint over lower-tier image generators when the job requires legible in-image text, 4K fidelity, or consistent character identity across multiple generations; the $0.15 flat rate only makes sense at those use cases.

<a id="veo-3-0-fast"></a>
### Veo 3.0 fast

- **Slug:** `veo-3-0-fast` · **Modell:** `veo-3.0-fast-generate-001` · **Kategori:** Video
- **Pris:** $0.15 per anrop · **Max bilder in:** 1 · **Aktiv:** ja
- **Beskrivning:** Veo 3.0 Fast Generate is Google's high-speed AI video model designed for rapid iteration, prototyping, and cost-efficient production. It is a variant of the standard Veo 3 model, optimized to generate 8-second video clips significantly faster—roughly in half the time—while retaining high visual quality (92-99% of standard quality)
- **Konfiguration** (`workflow_json`, utom modell):

  ```json
  {
    "prompt": "",
    "response_type": "video"
  }
  ```

**Parametrar:**

- `aspect_ratio` · default `16:9` · värden: `16:9`, `9:16` — Aspect ratio of the generated video
- `duration` · default `4` · värden: `4`, `6`, `8` — Video duration in seconds (1080p and 4k require duration=8)
- `negative_prompt` — Elements or styles to exclude from the generated video
- `PROMPT` · **obligatorisk** — Text prompt for the Gemini model
- `resolution` · default `720p` · värden: `720p`, `1080p`, `4k` — Video resolution (1080p and 4k require duration=8)

**AI context:**

> Prefer this endpoint over standard Veo 3 when turnaround time or cost matters more than marginal quality — the speed advantage is most noticeable during prompt iteration. The hard constraint to remember: `resolution=1080p` or `resolution=4k` **requires** `duration=8`; mixing either high resolution with `duration=4` or `duration=6` will error. For prototyping, `720p` + `duration=4` is the fastest and cheapest combination. `negative_prompt` is worth using — it meaningfully steers output away from unwanted motion styles, artifacts, or subject elements, especially at shorter durations where the model has less time to "correct" early-frame drift. `aspect_ratio` is the only layout control, so choose `9:16` upfront for vertical/social content rather than cropping post-generation. Image input can anchor the first frame or overall scene composition, but prompt text still drives motion and style; a weak prompt with a strong image typically produces sluggish or static-looking output.

> - Prefer this endpoint over image-to-video alternatives when you want high-fidelity, physics-aware scene generation from scratch; when you have a reference image to animate, pass it as an image input alongside the prompt rather than using a separate endpoint.

<a id="flux-fill-pro"></a>
### Flux Fill Pro

- **Slug:** `flux-fill-pro` · **Modell:** `black-forest-labs/flux-fill-pro` · **Kategori:** Image Generation
- **Pris:** $0.055 per anrop · **Max bilder in:** 4 · **Aktiv:** ja
- **Beskrivning:** Professional inpainting and outpainting model with state-of-the-art performance. Edit or extend images with natural, seamless results.
- **Konfiguration** (`workflow_json`, utom modell):

  ```json
  {
    "input": {
      "steps": 50,
      "prompt": "",
      "guidance": 60,
      "outpaint": "None",

      "safety_tolerance": 2,
      "prompt_upsampling": false
    },
    "image_field": "image",
    "response_type": "image",
    "image_field_type": "string"
  }
  ```

**Parametrar:**

- `guidance` · default `60` — Controls the balance between adherence to the text prompt and image quality/diversity. Higher values make the output more closely match the prompt but may reduce overall image quality. Lower values allow for more creative freedom but might produce results less relevant to the prompt.
- `mask` — A black-and-white image that describes the part of the image to inpaint. Black areas will be preserved while white areas will be inpainted. Must have the same size as image. Optional if you provide an alpha mask in the original image. Must be jpeg, png, gif, or webp.
- `outpaint` · default `None` · värden: `None`, `Zoom out 1.5x`, `Zoom out 2x`, `Make square`, `Left outpaint`, `Right outpaint`, `Top outpaint`, `Bottom outpaint` — A quick option for outpainting an input image. Mask will be ignored.
- `output_format` · default `jpg` · värden: `jpg`, `png` — Format of the output images.
- `prompt` · **obligatorisk** — Text prompt for image generation
- `prompt_upsampling` · default `false` — Automatically modify the prompt for more creative generation
- `safety_tolerance` · default `2` — Safety tolerance, 1 is most strict and 6 is most permissive
- `seed` — Random seed. Set for reproducible generation
- `steps` · default `50` — Number of diffusion steps. Higher values yield finer details but increase processing time.

**AI context:**

> Backed by `black-forest-labs/flux-fill-pro` on Replicate. The `guidance` default of 60 is unusually high compared to most diffusion models (where 7–12 is typical) — this model operates on a different scale, and values in the 30–80 range are the practical working band; going above 80 tends to over-sharpen or produce artifacts. `steps` is fixed at 50 in the workflow config and rarely needs changing — lowering it below ~30 noticeably degrades inpaint blending quality. When using `outpaint`, the `mask` parameter is ignored entirely, so don't ask users to provide one. Prefer this endpoint over general image generation when the task is editing a specific region of an existing image or extending canvas edges; for pure text-to-image work, a cheaper endpoint is more appropriate. Use `format: png` when the source image has transparency or the mask needs to be pixel-precise; jpg is fine for photographic content. Set `seed` any time a user wants to iterate on prompt wording while holding the inpaint region constant — it ensures structural consistency across runs.

  ```json
    "response_type": "image",
    "image_field_type": "string"
  }
  ```

**Parametrar:**

- `compression_quality` · default `80` — Compression quality for output (1-100)
- `upscale_factor` · default `x2` · värden: `x2`, `x4` — Factor by which to upscale the image

**AI context:**

> Backed by `google/upscaler` on Replicate. The `text` input accepted by the pipeline is not used by this model — only the image matters. `compression_quality` at the default of 80 is a reasonable balance; go above 90 only when the output will be further edited or printed, as file size grows quickly with minimal perceptible gain below 95. Prefer `x2` unless the source image is genuinely small (e.g., thumbnails or heavily compressed web images), since `x4` on an already-decent image can introduce softening or AI artifacts and costs the same flat $0.025. This endpoint is the right pick over generic upscalers when you need a single-step, no-tuning solution — there are no style, prompt, or creativity parameters to configure. If an upload is rejected, check that the source image isn't already large; some Replicate-hosted models have pixel dimension caps that can silently fail on oversized inputs.

<a id="sam3-image"></a>
### Sam3 Image

- **Slug:** `sam3-image` · **Modell:** `mattsays/sam3-image` · **Kategori:** Utilities
- **Pris:** $0.02 per anrop · **Max bilder in:** 1 · **Aktiv:** ja
- **Beskrivning:** Harness Meta's Segment Anything 3 (SAM) framework for zero-shot, pixel-perfect object segmentation. Isolate items, generate masks, or track elements across frames using natural language or coordinate prompts.
- **Konfiguration** (`workflow_json`, utom modell):

  ```json
  {
    "input": {
      "prompt": "person",
      "mask_only": false,
      "threshold": 0.5,
      "mask_color": "green",
      "return_zip": true,
      "mask_opacity": 0.5,
      "save_overlay": false
    },
    "image_field": "image",
    "response_type": "video",
    "image_field_type": "string"
  }
  ```

**Parametrar:**

- `mask_color` · default `green` — Color of the mask overlay. Options: 'green', 'red', 'blue', 'yellow', 'cyan', 'magenta'
- `mask_only` · default `true` — If True, returns a black-and-white mask image instead of an overlay on the original image
- `mask_opacity` · default `0.5` — Opacity of the mask overlay (0.0 to 1.0)
- `prompt` · default `person` — Text prompt for segmentation
- `return_zip` · default `false` — If True, returns a ZIP file containing individual masks as PNGs
- `save_overlay` · default `false` — If True, includes the overlay image in the ZIP file
- `threshold` · default `0.5` — Confidence threshold for object detection

**AI context:**

> Despite the `response_type` being "video," this endpoint returns a static image (or ZIP of PNGs) — the video type is a Replicate artifact wrapper, not an animation. The workflow config ships with `return_zip: true` but the parameter schema defaults to `false`; the config value wins, so users will receive a ZIP by default unless they explicitly override it. `mask_only` defaults to `false` in the config (overlay mode), overriding the schema's `true` — expect a colored overlay on the original image out of the box, not a clean B&W mask. For clean cutouts or downstream compositing, flip `mask_only: true` and `return_zip: true` to get individual PNG masks without the original blended in. `threshold` is worth tuning (0.3–0.7 is the practical range): lower values catch partial/occluded objects but increase false positives; above 0.7 it frequently misses smaller targets. `mask_opacity` and `mask_color` only affect output when `mask_only` is `false`, so leave them at defaults if you're working with masks directly. Prefer this endpoint over general object-detection pipelines when you need pixel-level masks rather than bounding boxes, or when the target object class isn't in a fixed label set.

<a id="dremina-seedance-2-00"></a>
### Dremina Seedance 2.00

- **Slug:** `dremina-seedance-2-00` · **Modell:** `bytedance/seedance-2.0` · **Kategori:** Video
- **Pris:** $1 per anrop · **Max bilder in:** 1 · **Aktiv:** ja
- **Beskrivning:** a second-generation, multimodal AI video generation model released in early 2026. It allows creators to generate cinematic-quality videos up to 15 seconds long (typically 5-12 seconds) using text, image, video, and audio inputs. It is highly regarded for its strong temporal consistency, meaning characters and objects maintain their appearance across frames, and its ability to handle complex camera movements like pans, tilts, and zooms
- **Konfiguration** (`workflow_json`, utom modell):

  ```json
  {
    "input": {
      "prompt": "",
      "duration": 5,
      "resolution": "720p",
      "aspect_ratio": "16:9",
      "generate_audio": true,
      "reference_audios": [],
      "reference_images": [],
      "reference_videos": []
    },
    "image_field": "image",
    "response_type": "video",
    "image_field_type": "string"
  }
  ```

**Parametrar:**

- `aspect_ratio` · default `16:9` · värden: `16:9`, `4:3`, `1:1`, `3:4`, `9:16`, `21:9`, `9:21`, `adaptive` — Video aspect ratio. Set to 'adaptive' to let the model choose the best ratio based on inputs.
- `duration` · default `5` — Video duration in seconds (Max 15) - Set to -1 for intelligent duration (model picks the best length).
- `generate_audio` · default `true` — Generate synchronized audio with the video, including dialogue (use double quotes in prompt), sound effects, and background music.
- `last_frame_image` — Input image for last frame generation. Only works if a first frame image is also provided. Cannot be combined with reference images.
- `prompt` · **obligatorisk** — Text prompt for video generation
- `reference_audios` — Reference audio files (up to 3, total duration max 15s) for audio-driven generation and lip-sync. Requires at least one reference image or video. Reference them in your prompt as [Audio1], [Audio2], etc.
- `reference_images` — Reference images (up to 9) for character consistency, style guidance, and scene composition. Cannot be used together with first/last frame images. You can reference them in your prompt as [Image1], [Image2], etc.
- `reference_videos` — Reference videos (up to 3, total duration max 15s) for motion transfer, style reference, and editing. Reference them in your prompt as [Video1], [Video2], etc.
- `resolution` · default `720p` · värden: `480p`, `720p`, `1080p` — Video resolution.
- `seed` — Random seed. Set for reproducible generation.

**AI context:**

> Backed by ByteDance's Seedance 2.0 on Replicate. The `duration` default of 5s is conservative — set to `-1` to let the model pick the optimal length, which tends to produce better pacing for complex prompts; the hard cap is 15s. Use `aspect_ratio: adaptive` when supplying a reference image or video so the output ratio matches the input rather than forcing a crop. `reference_images` (up to 9) are the primary lever for character/style consistency, but they're mutually exclusive with `first_frame` (`image` field) and `last_frame_image` — choose one approach per request. For lip-sync or audio-driven generation, supply `reference_audios` alongside at least one reference image or video, and explicitly tag sources in the prompt as `[Audio1]`, `[Image1]`, etc. — the model ignores untagged references. `generate_audio` is on by default and adds cost/latency; disable it for silent clips or when you're supplying your own audio in post. `seed` is worth pinning once you find a good result — temporal consistency is strong, but prompt-identical runs without a seed will still vary noticeably in camera movement and scene composition.

**Parametrar:**

- `aspect_ratio` · default `auto` · värden: `auto`, `16:9`, `4:3`, `1:1`, `9:16`, `3:4`, `3:2`, `2:3` — Aspect ratio of the video. For text-to-video, defaults to 16:9. For image-to-video, defaults to the input image's native aspect ratio. Ignored when editing a video.

> - `aspect_ratio: auto` is the right default for image-to-video — overriding it can cause cropping or letterboxing if the input image isn't that ratio.
> - At $1.00 flat, this is on the pricier end of the platform's video category; prefer it when output quality and the xAI model specifically are the requirement, not just "any video generation."
> - Input video for editing must be a **direct file URL** (not a redirect or HTML page); mp4 is the safest format — webm support can be inconsistent depending on codec.
